title: Sorting
definition: Sorting rearranges elements of a sequence into a specified order (e.g. ascending).
intuition: Organized datasets are significantly easier to search and process.
how_it_works: Algorithms use comparisons (Quick, Merge, Heap) or distribution (Bucket, Radix, Counting) keys.
when_to_use: When preprocessing datasets for binary search, grouping, or greedy operations.
when_not_to_use: When dataset is already sorted or operations are O(1) hash-based.
common_mistakes: Using unstable sort when stability is required
Using O(n^2) sort when O(n log n) is feasible
complexity: Comparison: Best O(n log n), Non-comparison: O(n)
content: Sorting rearranges elements of a sequence into a specified order (e.g. ascending).
